entities.name: PMID:25080971
observations: 2014 study integrated transcriptomic and quantitative proteomic profiles after PDGF-BB stimulation in primary human bladder smooth muscle cells.
The study reported a novel PDGF-MYC network and described itself as the first systems-level analysis of the PDGF-regulated transcriptome and proteome in normal smooth muscle cells.

entities.name: Human bladder smooth muscle cells
observations: Primary human bladder smooth muscle cells were treated with 1 nM PDGF-BB for 0, 4, or 24 hours using transcriptomic profiling and triplex-SILAC quantitative proteomics.

entities.name: PDGF-MYC network
observations: Integrated PDGF-responsive data identified MYC as the most highly networked master regulator; the signature was associated with smooth-muscle-cell proliferation, migration, and angiogenesis.

entities.name: MYC
observations: PDGF treatment changed 1,695 genes and 241 proteins, with 40 concordant mRNA/protein targets; MYC was the most highly networked regulator. MYC inhibition reduced PDGF-associated smooth-muscle-cell proliferation and migration.

entities.name: DIAPH3
observations: DIAPH3 was identified as a previously unrecognized PDGF-responsive target regulated by MYC and JUN and required for PDGF-stimulated lamellipodium formation.
